author: Theikosh
quote: 13 years of waiting for a glorified chore **** a game that took over a decade to arrive, GTA 6 is one of the most disappointing gaming experiences I’ve had in years. The graphics are incredible, the world is massive, and the attention to detail is impressive. But once you look past the visuals, you start realizing how little Rockstar has actually improved where it **** protagonists are a massive downgrade.Jason has absolutely zero personality. He’s boring, forgettable, and feels more like Lucia’s personal assistant than an actual GTA protagonist. Compare him to Niko Bellic, Trevor, Michael, or Arthur Morgan. Those characters had depth, memorable dialogue, and personalities that made you want to keep playing. Jason is just there.Lucia is somehow even worse. She’s annoying as ****, her voice gets on my nerves, and I genuinely struggle to understand why I’m supposed to care about her. Her questionable decisions as a mother are brushed aside far too easily by Jason, making their entire relationship feel poorly **** speaking of their relationship, why the **** am I being forced to maintain it?Rockstar made it sound like the relationship mechanics would be optional, yet the story keeps pushing me into domestic activities and running errands for Lucia. I’m playing Grand Theft Auto, not Boyfriend Simulator 2026. I didn’t wait over a decade to play as some beta cuck doing chores and buying **** story is mediocre at **** pacing is painfully slow, the dialogue is forgettable, and the supporting characters barely leave an impression. Previous Rockstar games had side characters who were sometimes more entertaining than the protagonists themselves. Here, most of them feel like **** missions aren’t much better. Rockstar is still obsessed with overly scripted sequences where you follow someone, listen to endless dialogue, drive somewhere, watch a cutscene, and repeat. There’s barely any room for **** game constantly tells you exactly what to do and punishes you for deviating from its intended path. For a franchise supposedly built around freedom, that’s **** open world looks next-gen, but the freedom doesn’t feel **** interactions don’t feel like the revolutionary leap I expected after Red Dead Redemption 2. Sure, people react to things, the streets feel alive, and the animations look incredible. But where’s the meaningful interaction?Why can’t I befriend random NPCs? Why can’t I build relationships with people I meet around the city? Why can’t I flirt with or seduce random characters, have casual hookups, or develop my own social experiences?I’m not expecting every NPC to have an entire storyline, but after all these years, I expected Rockstar to push the boundaries of what an open world actually allows you to do.Instead, we get a beautiful world with surprisingly limited player **** when did GTA become so obsessed with realism that it forgot to be fun?Weapon restrictions, tedious management mechanics, errands, slow progression, and unnecessarily complicated systems don’t automatically make a game immersive. Sometimes they just make it **** Dead Redemption 2 could get away with its slower, more deliberate gameplay because it had an incredible story and characters worth investing in. GTA 6 borrows that philosophy without delivering the same emotional payoff.Even the shooting feels unnecessarily clunky at times. The controls can feel awkward, and the gameplay still carries some of Rockstar’s outdated design **** where’s the classic GTA personality?The absurd humor, the memorable psychos, the ridiculous situations, the ruthless satire of American culture, all the things that made GTA feel different from every other open-world game seem toned down. The game takes itself far too seriously while failing to deliver a story compelling enough to justify that **** biggest issue is that GTA 6 seems more interested in simulating everyday life than letting me escape it.I don’t play GTA to do household chores, maintain a forced relationship, or sit through endless conversations with characters I don’t care about.I play GTA for freedom, memorable characters, crime, chaos, and the ability to do things I can’t do in real **** somehow, despite having one of the most detailed open worlds ever created, GTA 6 still feels unnecessarily restrictive. Final verdict: 0.5/10. Rockstar has created a technological masterpiece wrapped around a mediocre story, unlikable protagonists, outdated mission design, and gameplay that frequently mistakes inconvenience for **** world is impressive. The graphics are phenomenal. But a beautiful map isn’t enough to make a great game.13 years of waiting, and somehow the most revolutionary thing about GTA 6 is how realistic doing chores has become.
